item.content:encoded:
You know, whether or not the object for itself is meh, this is a good example of how to add story to an object, and still keep the total article relatively short. I'd actually like to remember this one as an example for new writers of what is needed for a good article. It's not too ambitious, with addendum after addendum. It shows why the story is more important than the anomaly.

It feels like the sort of article you can point to, to say, you can do this.

+1. I like this.

item.content:encoded:
I continuously marvel at the people this and some other scips despict: they are normal scientist or whatever that discover incredible things… just to go and use them for something completely retarded (TELEPORTATION!… for trampolines?). It just… doesn't make sense: If someone made a completely groundbreaking gamechanger development like that the last, really, the last thing they would think about would be to use it for revamping a damn trampolin! It's like a take at Looney Toons logic in real life.

However, I liked the report, so I'm giving it an upvote [Double standards? Where?]

item.title: I am not a fan
item.content:encoded: For starters, with those comments about office rumours and teleportation research the tone doesn't feel clinical enough. Furthermore, things such as why bullets do not trigger the effect are simply stated but never elaborated upon. item.title: Usage
item.content:encoded: More of a note for future reference than anything else - if necessary, it seems SCP-176 could be utilized as part of an effective "bunker buster" type weapon - in some other SCP requires termination by explosive or other large ordinance but is too dangerous to unseal from its 15-m-thick-walled containment zone. Not a very likely or common usage, perhaps, but something to keep in mind as an option.
